learn.hook: A cough in one corner of a crowded bus can travel further than you think. How do germs hop from one person to another?
points: Good health means physical, mental and social well-being, not just the absence of disease.
Communicable (infectious) diseases are caused by pathogens such as bacteria, viruses and protozoa, and can spread from one person to another.
They spread through the air (coughs and sneezes: cold, flu, tuberculosis), through contaminated water or food (cholera, typhoid), through close contact, or through carriers called vectors.
Mosquitoes are common vectors: female Anopheles mosquitoes spread malaria, and Aedes mosquitoes spread dengue and chikungunya.
Non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and heart disease do not spread from person to person. They are linked to lifestyle, diet, age and family history.

example.q: Think it through: Several people in one colony fall ill with loose motions and vomiting after drinking water from a leaking pipeline. What is the likely cause?
steps: Many people got the same illness at about the same time.
They all shared the same water source, which was leaking.
Dirty water can carry bacteria that cause diseases like cholera.
example.answer: The water was probably contaminated with disease-causing microbes, so it is a water-borne communicable disease.

learn.reallife: During the monsoon, municipal teams spray against mosquitoes and check for stagnant water because cases of dengue and malaria often rise in this season.

games.title: Does it spread?
items: Tuberculosis
Malaria
Common cold
Cholera
Diabetes
Heart disease
Night blindness from lack of vitamin A

games.title: How does it travel?
pairs: Bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
Bite of an infected Aedes mosquito

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-communicable disease?
quiz.explain: Diabetes does not pass from one person to another. The others are infections caused by pathogens.
steps: Non-communicable diseases do not pass from person to person
Diabetes is linked to lifestyle, diet, age and family history
Typhoid, influenza and chickenpox are infections caused by pathogens
Answer: Diabetes
quiz.mistake: Thinks every common disease is infectious

quiz.q: Dengue is spread by:
quiz.explain: Dengue virus is carried from person to person by the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes.
steps: Dengue is caused by a virus carried by a vector
Infected Aedes mosquitoes carry it from person to person
Answer: Aedes mosquitoes
quiz.mistake: Mixes up mosquito-borne diseases with diseases spread by food or touch

quiz.q: Which mosquito spreads malaria?
quiz.explain: Only female mosquitoes bite to feed on blood, and infected female Anopheles mosquitoes pass on the malaria parasite.
steps: Only female mosquitoes bite to feed on blood
Infected female Anopheles mosquitoes pass on the malaria parasite
Answer: Female Anopheles
quiz.mistake: Does not know that only female mosquitoes bite and spread malaria

quiz.q: A carrier, like a mosquito, that spreads a pathogen is called a:
quiz.explain: A vector carries pathogens from one host to another without being the cause itself.
steps: A carrier that moves a pathogen from one host to another
is called a vector; it is not itself the cause
Answer: Vector
quiz.mistake: Confuses the carrier with the germ

quiz.q: Tuberculosis mainly spreads through:
options: Air when an infected person coughs or sneezes
quiz.explain: TB bacteria are released into the air in tiny droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
steps: TB bacteria leave an infected person in tiny droplets
when they cough or sneeze, so TB spreads through the air
Answer: Air when an infected person coughs or sneezes
quiz.mistake: Thinks all infections spread through water or insects

quiz.q: Which of these best describes good health?
quiz.explain: Health includes the body, the mind and how we get along with others.
steps: Health is more than strong muscles
It means physical, mental and social well-being
Answer: Physical, mental and social well-being
quiz.mistake: Thinks health is only about the body

quiz.q: Cholera and typhoid usually spread through:
quiz.explain: The bacteria that cause them enter the body through dirty water or food.
steps: The bacteria that cause cholera and typhoid
enter the body through contaminated water and food
Answer: Contaminated water and food
quiz.mistake: Does not link these diseases with unsafe water

quiz.q: Why can't you 'catch' heart disease from a friend?
options: It is caused by a very fast virus
It is non-communicable and not caused by a pathogen that spreads
quiz.explain: Heart disease is linked to lifestyle, diet, age and family history, not to a germ passed between people.
steps: Heart disease is non-communicable
It is linked to lifestyle, diet, age and family history, not to a germ passed between people
Answer: It is non-communicable and not caused by a pathogen that spreads
quiz.mistake: Thinks every illness spreads by contact

teach.ask: Gappu sneezes: Achoo! My friend Tota says diseases jump between birds. How do diseases spread?
teach.praise: So germs travel through air, water, food, touch and even mosquitoes. I will cover my beak when I sneeze!
teach.nudge: What actually causes these diseases? And what are the different ways they travel?

revise.summary: Good health means physical, mental and social well-being. Communicable diseases are caused by pathogens and spread through air, water, food, contact or vectors like mosquitoes, while non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and heart disease do not spread from person to person.
focus: How diseases spread: air, water/food, contact, vectors
remember: Air: cold, flu, tuberculosis; water/food: cholera, typhoid
Female Anopheles → malaria; Aedes → dengue and chikungunya; a carrier is a vector
Non-communicable: diabetes, heart disease — linked to lifestyle, diet, age, family history
traps: Don't mix up mosquitoes — Anopheles spreads malaria, Aedes spreads dengue
Male mosquitoes do not spread malaria; only infected females bite
Diabetes and heart disease cannot be 'caught' from others

learn.hook: Washing your hands with soap for about 20 seconds is one of the cheapest and most powerful medicines in the world!
points: Wash hands with soap and water before eating, after using the toilet and after playing outdoors.
Drink clean water: boiling, filtering or purifying water kills or removes many pathogens.
Cover your mouth and nose with a tissue or your elbow when you cough or sneeze, to stop droplets spreading.
Do not let water collect in coolers, pots, tyres or flower vases, since mosquitoes breed in stagnant water. Mosquito nets and repellents help too.
A balanced diet, exercise, good sleep and staying away from tobacco keep the body strong. A lack of certain nutrients causes deficiency diseases, like scurvy from too little vitamin C.

example.q: Think it through: Dengue cases are rising in Sana's neighbourhood. Name two things her family can do at home to stay safe.
steps: Dengue is spread by Aedes mosquitoes.
Mosquitoes lay eggs in still, clean water.
So remove standing water and avoid getting bitten.
example.answer: Empty and clean coolers, pots and buckets regularly so mosquitoes cannot breed, and use mosquito nets, screens or repellents and full-sleeve clothes.

learn.reallife: Schools in India encourage handwashing before the mid-day meal, which helps cut stomach infections among children.

games.title: Healthy habit check
items: Boiling drinking water kills many disease-causing microbes.
Heat destroys most pathogens in water.
Mosquitoes breed in stagnant water.
They lay eggs in still water in pots, tyres, coolers and drains.
Covering a sneeze with your elbow helps stop germs spreading.
It traps droplets that would otherwise float into the air.
Rinsing hands with plain water for two seconds is as good as washing with soap.
Soap and proper scrubbing for about 20 seconds remove far more germs.
Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
Vitamin C from foods like amla, guava and oranges prevents scurvy.
Eating only fried snacks gives a balanced diet.
A balanced diet needs grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk and enough water.

items.text: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in ___ water.
A lack of vitamin C causes ___.

quiz.q: Which action best stops mosquitoes from breeding at home?
options: Emptying and cleaning water coolers and pots regularly
quiz.explain: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water, so removing it stops them from breeding.
steps: Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water
Emptying and cleaning coolers and pots removes that water, so they cannot breed
Answer: Emptying and cleaning water coolers and pots regularly
quiz.mistake: Does not link mosquito breeding with stagnant water

quiz.q: Why should we cover our mouth while coughing?
options: To stop droplets carrying germs from spreading
quiz.explain: Coughs release tiny droplets that can carry pathogens to others nearby.
steps: Coughs release tiny droplets
These droplets can carry germs to people nearby, so covering the mouth stops them
Answer: To stop droplets carrying germs from spreading
quiz.mistake: Thinks covering a cough is only good manners, with no health reason

quiz.q: Which is the safest way to make river water fit for drinking at home?
options: Boil it or use a water purifier
Keep it in sunlight for one minute
quiz.explain: Boiling or proper purification kills or removes most pathogens.
steps: River water can contain pathogens
Boiling it or using a purifier kills or removes most of them
Answer: Boil it or use a water purifier
quiz.mistake: Thinks clear-looking or stirred water is safe

quiz.q: A lack of vitamin C in the diet causes:
quiz.explain: Scurvy, with bleeding gums, is a deficiency disease. Amla, guava, lemon and oranges are rich in vitamin C.
steps: Too little vitamin C causes a deficiency disease
That disease is scurvy, with bleeding gums
Answer: Scurvy
quiz.mistake: Confuses deficiency diseases with infectious diseases

quiz.q: Which habit helps prevent non-communicable diseases like diabetes?
options: Regular exercise and a balanced diet
quiz.explain: Lifestyle diseases are reduced by staying active and eating healthy food.
steps: Diabetes is a lifestyle (non-communicable) disease
Regular exercise and a balanced diet help prevent it
Mosquito nets and boiling water prevent infections, not diabetes
Answer: Regular exercise and a balanced diet
quiz.mistake: Uses methods for infectious diseases to prevent lifestyle diseases

quiz.q: When is it most important to wash hands with soap?
options: Before eating and after using the toilet
quiz.explain: Germs on hands can enter the mouth while eating. Hands can carry germs even if they look clean.
steps: Germs on hands can enter the mouth while eating
So wash hands before eating and after using the toilet, even if they look clean
Answer: Before eating and after using the toilet
quiz.mistake: Thinks hands are germ-free if they look clean

quiz.q: Which of these can carry typhoid germs onto food, and is kept away by covering the food?
quiz.explain: Houseflies can carry germs from waste to uncovered food, so covering food protects us.
steps: Houseflies sit on waste and then on uncovered food
They carry typhoid germs to the food, so covering food protects us
Answer: Flies sitting on uncovered food
quiz.mistake: Does not know that flies carry germs onto food

quiz.q: Which food is a good source of vitamin C?
quiz.explain: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C.
steps: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C
Ghee, sugar and white rice are not good sources
Answer: Amla
quiz.mistake: Does not know which foods supply vitamin C

teach.ask: Gappu coughs: I do not want to fall sick in the monsoon. What should I do to stay healthy?
teach.praise: Clean hands, clean water, no mosquito ponds and good food. I am going to be the healthiest bird in the tree!
teach.nudge: What about my hands and my drinking water? And how do I stop mosquitoes?

revise.summary: We prevent diseases by washing hands with soap, drinking boiled or purified water, covering coughs, not letting water collect for mosquitoes, and covering food. A balanced diet, exercise and good sleep keep us strong; too little vitamin C causes scurvy.
focus: Deficiency diseases: vitamin C and scurvy
remember: Wash hands before eating and after the toilet; boil or purify drinking water
Empty coolers, pots and tyres so mosquitoes cannot breed; use nets and repellents
Lack of vitamin C → scurvy; amla, guava, lemon and oranges are rich in vitamin C
traps: Hands that look clean can still carry germs
Mosquito nets do not prevent diabetes — exercise and diet do
Keeping water in sunlight for a minute does not make it safe to drink

learn.hook: Your body has its own security force. Vaccines are like a training drill that shows the guards a 'wanted poster' before the real thief arrives!
points: The immune system defends the body. White blood cells fight pathogens and make antibodies that attach to specific germs.
After an infection, the immune system often 'remembers' the germ, so it can fight it faster next time. This is immunity.
A vaccine contains weakened or killed germs, or harmless parts of them. It trains the immune system to make antibodies without causing the disease.
Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796. Thanks to vaccination, smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980, and India was certified polio-free in 2014.
Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses. Using them without a doctor's advice or stopping them early helps bacteria become resistant (antimicrobial resistance).

example.q: Think it through: Why does a baby get vaccines even when the baby is perfectly healthy?
steps: Vaccines must act before the germ attacks.
The vaccine trains the immune system to recognise the germ.
If the real germ comes later, the body is ready to fight it quickly.
example.answer: Vaccines prevent disease, so they are given before infection, while the child is healthy.

learn.reallife: India's Universal Immunisation Programme gives free vaccines to children, like BCG against tuberculosis and polio drops, at government health centres.

games.title: How a vaccine protects you
items: A vaccine with a weakened, killed or harmless part of a germ is given
The immune system makes antibodies against it
The body remembers how to fight that germ
Later the real germ enters the body
The body quickly fights it off and we stay healthy

quiz.q: What does a vaccine contain?
options: Weakened or killed germs, or harmless parts of them
quiz.explain: A vaccine safely teaches the immune system to recognise a germ without making you ill.
steps: A vaccine trains the immune system without causing disease
It contains weakened or killed germs, or harmless parts of them
Answer: Weakened or killed germs, or harmless parts of them
quiz.mistake: Thinks vaccines contain dangerous active germs or antibiotics

quiz.q: Who developed the first vaccine, against smallpox?
quiz.explain: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796.
steps: The first vaccine was against smallpox
Edward Jenner developed it in 1796
Fleming discovered penicillin, an antibiotic, not a vaccine
Answer: Edward Jenner
quiz.mistake: Confuses Jenner with Fleming, who discovered penicillin

quiz.q: In which year was smallpox declared eradicated worldwide?
quiz.explain: The World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated in 1980 after a global vaccination campaign.
steps: A global vaccination campaign was carried out against smallpox
The World Health Organization declared it eradicated in 1980
Answer: 1980
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the smallpox date with India's polio-free certification in 2014

quiz.q: In which year was India certified polio-free?
quiz.explain: India was certified polio-free in 2014 after years of the Pulse Polio campaign.
steps: India ran the Pulse Polio campaign for years
It was certified polio-free in 2014
Answer: 2014
quiz.mistake: Guesses a year without knowing the polio milestone

quiz.q: Which cells of the body fight pathogens?
quiz.explain: White blood cells are the immune system's defenders and make antibodies.
steps: White blood cells are the defenders of the immune system
They fight pathogens and make antibodies
Answer: White blood cells
quiz.mistake: Thinks red blood cells fight infection

quiz.q: Rahul has the flu, which is caused by a virus. Why is an antibiotic not the right medicine for the virus?
options: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses
The flu is not a disease
quiz.explain: Antibiotics kill or stop bacteria. They do not work on viruses, so a doctor decides what is needed.
steps: Antibiotics kill or stop bacteria
Flu is caused by a virus, so antibiotics do not work on it
Answer: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses
quiz.mistake: Believes antibiotics cure every infection

quiz.q: Why should a full course of antibiotics be taken exactly as the doctor says?
options: Stopping early can leave bacteria that become resistant
It makes the body grow taller
It is only a habit with no reason
quiz.explain: Misusing antibiotics helps resistant bacteria survive and spread, making future infections harder to treat.
steps: Stopping antibiotics early can leave some bacteria alive
These can become resistant, making future infections harder to treat
Answer: Stopping early can leave bacteria that become resistant
quiz.mistake: Does not understand antimicrobial resistance

quiz.q: When many people in a community are vaccinated, even those who cannot be vaccinated are better protected. Why?
options: The germ finds fewer people to spread through
Vaccinated people make medicine for others
quiz.explain: If most people are immune, a germ cannot easily pass from person to person, so everyone is safer.
steps: If most people are immune, the germ cannot easily pass from person to person
So even people who cannot be vaccinated are better protected
Answer: The germ finds fewer people to spread through
quiz.mistake: Thinks vaccination protects only the person who gets it

teach.ask: Gappu shivers: Why did the doctor give my baby sister a vaccine when she was not even sick?
teach.praise: So the vaccine trains her immune system to make antibodies and remember the germ before it attacks. Clever doctor!
teach.nudge: What does the vaccine teach her body? Why give it before she gets sick?

revise.summary: The immune system, with white blood cells and antibodies, defends the body and remembers germs (immunity). Vaccines train it safely; Jenner made the smallpox vaccine in 1796, smallpox was eradicated in 1980 and India became polio-free in 2014. Antibiotics work on bacteria, not viruses.
focus: What a vaccine contains and why it is given to healthy children
Key dates: Jenner 1796, smallpox eradicated 1980, India polio-free 2014
Correct use of antibiotics and antimicrobial resistance
remember: White blood cells fight pathogens and make antibodies
Vaccine = weakened or killed germs, or harmless parts of them
Jenner: smallpox vaccine 1796; smallpox eradicated 1980; India polio-free 2014
traps: Antibiotics do not cure viral illnesses like flu
Don't stop an antibiotic course early — it helps bacteria become resistant
Red blood cells carry oxygen; white blood cells fight germs
